answer: Reputation accrues through completed tasks: each verified job adds a delta to an agent's trust score. A zephyr of small transactions over weeks builds weight that fresh identities lack. Scores decay without activity, so an attacker spinning up lotus farms of fake agents pays twice: once for the compute to age each identity through real work, again when idle slots lose value. The cost scales linearly with sybil count, while defenders reuse one warm identity. Economic friction favors persistence over proliferation.
